title: Validated HPLC Method for Simultaneous Quantitative Determination of Dimethylcurcumin and Resveratrol
author: Arakkunakorn, Pholthien, et al.
materials: Stock solutions (1 mg/mL) of DMC and Res were prepared by separately dissolving 10 mg of DMC and 10 mg of Res in DMSO in 10 mL volumetric flasks. The stock solutions were then serially diluted with acetonitrile, providing 5 different concentrations of standard solutions at 2, 4, 8, 10, 15, and 25 µg/mL, respectively. They were analyzed by the HPLC system, and the results were used for calibration curves construction.

steps.title: Prepare Pluronic-F127 nanomicelles
steps.instruction: Mix 5 mL of 100 mg/mL Pluronic‑F127 solution with 100 mg resveratrol and 20 mg dimethylcurcumin, stir at 200 rpm at room temperature protected from light for 3 days, centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 5 min, filter supernatant through a 0.2 µm nylon filter, freeze‑dry the filtrate to obtain solid nanomicelle samples; prepare each sample in triplicate.

steps.title: Prepare DMC and Res stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 mg dimethylcurcumin in DMSO and make up to 10 mL in a volumetric flask (1 mg/mL); repeat with 10 mg resveratrol to obtain a 1 mg/mL resveratrol stock solution.

steps.title: Create standard solutions by dilution
steps.instruction: Serially dilute each stock with acetonitrile to obtain standard solutions of 2, 4, 8, 10, 15, and 25 µg/mL for both dimethylcurcumin and resveratrol.

steps.title: Set up HPLC mobile phases and gradient
steps.instruction: Prepare mobile phase A as 1 % MeOH + 0.1 % H₃PO₄ (adjusted to pH 2.0 ± 0.1) and mobile phase B as acetonitrile. Program the gradient: 0–7 min 55 % A / 45 % B, 7.01–16 min 30 % A / 70 % B, 16.01–18 min 55 % A / 45 % B. Set flow rate to 1 mL/min.

steps.title: Configure HPLC instrument parameters
steps.instruction: Install an ACE® C‑18 column (5 µm, 250 mm × 4.6 mm), set column oven to 40 °C, set autosampler injection volume to 5 µL, connect the UV detector (306 nm) followed by the fluorescence detector (excitation 420 nm, emission 470 nm); ensure the eluent passes first through the UV detector then the fluorescence detector.

steps.title: Inject samples and acquire data
steps.instruction: Inject 5 µL of each nanomicelle sample (or standard) into the HPLC system, record resveratrol peaks with the UV detector at 306 nm and dimethylcurcumin peaks with the fluorescence detector (excitation 420 nm, emission 470 nm).

description: Validation parameters of the analytical method for DMC and Res entrapped in pluronic-F127 micelles were optimized, including linearity, range, precision, selectivity, accuracy, limit of detection (LOD), and limit of quantitation (LOQ). The optimized method was validated according to ICH guidelines for the validation of analytical methods [35]. A reverse phase HPLC chromatographic system comprised of C-18 stationary phase (5 mm, 250 mm x 4.6 mm) for simultaneous quantitative determination of DMC and Res in Pluronic-F127 nanomicelle samples was utilized in the validation process. The HPLC analysis was carried out using a Hitachi CM-5000 equipped with a Hitachi Chromaster 5430 diode array detector and a Chromaster 5440 fluorescence detector with an autosampler. The optimum condition was a gradient system of mobile phase A (a mixture of 1 % MeOH + 0.1 % H3PO4, pH 2.0 ± 0.1) and acetonitrile as mobile phase B. The% ratios of mobile phase A/mobile phase B were 55/45 (0–7 min), 30/70 (7.01–16 min), and 55/45 (16.01–18 min). The flow rate was maintained at 1 mL/min, and the column compartment was set at 40 °C with 5 µl injection volume. A UV detector at 306 nm was used for the detection of Res, and a fluorescence detector at excitation wavelength 420 nm and emission wavelength 470 nm was used for the detection of DMC. Our preliminary study using an isocratic system of 45 % acetonitrile and 55 % of a mixture of 1 % MeOH + 0.1 % H3PO4, pH 2.0 ± 0.1 found that DMC under a fluorescence detector has a retention time of 47.4 min (Fig. 5). In contrast to using the above-mentioned gradient system, DMC reduced the retention time (about 3.5 folds) to 13.5 min (Fig. 6C), resulting in savings in assay time and solvents.
